AM13I-01.note: Two unit rates plus a dollars-to-cents conversion; all three distractors are real methods (64-oz rate alone, the marginal $4.24/24oz, and $4.24/64).

AM13I-02.note: Three direct steps, no decision to make.

AM13I-03.note: One product; 19,905.60 punishes assuming 52 weeks, 17,952 dropping the 40 cents.

AM13I-04.note: Both conversions must go the same direction; 5.29 is dividing by 1.15, 6.08 stopping at euros, 1.84 skipping the liters. Clean.

AM13I-06.note: Single proportion; only 405 (multiplying instead of dividing) is a method trap.

AM13I-07.note: Two conditions to carry (unfenced side, gateway); 702 is the full perimeter, 486 forgets the gate, 675 forgets the building side. Well built.

AM13I-08.note: Volume, density, then a subtraction from the limit; 8,448 is the mass itself and 3,720 uses density 1,000. The decimal product is the slowest part.

AM13I-09.note: Mass to length to a count, and the count must be floored, not rounded (25.7 to 25). 45 is the length, 8 skips the mass step.

AM13I-10.note: The good kind of hard: the natural first approach, 15+20=35, is exactly choice B, and 32.0 is the total fall mistaken for the needed rise. Requires 1/0.68, an inverse the stem never states.

AM13I-11.note: Natural first approach 180/1.25 = 144 sits on a distractor; the student must see budget/price is the invariant and then floor 151.2. Nothing is stated to set up.

AM13I-12.note: Two-rate mixture, then the extra step the stem asks for: kilometers, not hours. 121 is the distance at the other speed, 160 assumes an even time split, 132.5 half the total.
